title: Asking people for things

fn.en: Make polite requests, reply to them, and write a short email.

sub.en: Look at the requests. When do you say Can/Could YOU, and when Can/Could I?

items.q: You want your colleague to do something: ___ send me the file?
items.why: Can/Could YOU = I want you to do it.  Can/Could I = I want to do it myself.

items.q: You want to do something yourself: ___ open the window?

items.why: Would you like…? offers.  Do you like…? asks about taste in general.

items.q: Could you ___ me the salt, please?
items.why: can / could + the base form, with no “to”.

use: Can we use the computers after class?
tts: Hello and welcome, everyone. Before we begin, I’d like to tell you a few things about the course.
Excuse me. Could I open the window? — Yes, of course. It’s really hot in here, isn’t it?
So, class is at two p.m. every Thursday and Friday in the room next door. You can use the computers there. Yes, do you have a question?
Er, yes. Can we use the computers after class? — Yes, of course, but you need a password. It’s student451.

acts.title: Two emails
text: Thanks for your email. Could you send me the contract before Friday? I would also like to check the dates for the meeting in May.
Hi Marat! Thanks for calling back yesterday. Can you print the photos for the office? And could I borrow your camera at the weekend? Best wishes, Dana

write.q: Write a short email to a colleague: 5 lines. Open it, thank them for something, make two requests with Could you…? and Could I…?, and close it.
write.model: Dear Ms Petrova, Thanks for your email. Could you send me the contract before Friday, please? And could I have the dates for the May meeting? I need them for the team. Kind regards, Aidana Serik

speak.q: Say four requests out loud, one for each situation: at work, with a neighbour, in a shop and by phone. Then reply to two of them — one yes, one polite no.
speak.model: Could I open the window? Could I borrow some sugar? Could you show me a bigger size, please? Could you call back after three? — Of course you can. — I’m sorry, but that’s not possible today.
